approaches.name: unified national social registry and interoperable MIS for multi-program targeting
approaches.description: The project builds a single social registry and shared MIS, linked to civil registry and social security databases, to target households across programs. Practices: Unique social registry (RSU) for cross-program targeting; Common MIS platform overseeing multiple social programs; Nationwide RSU deployment with continuous data refresh; Common MIS platform across social programs and databases; Interoperable MIS linked to civil registry and social security databases; National unique social registry with proxy means testing and community validation; Unique social registry (RSU) registering households nationwide; Integrated social registry MIS for multi-program targeting; TA to build unified social registry (RSU) and its MIS.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: single registry shared across programs - cue: 'adaptive' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Besides quarterly cash transfers20, the program also provides economic inclusion measures to beneficiary households to support their income and build their resilience in view of their exit from the PTMP.21 In addition to financing the PTMP, the PFSP has also been supporting the development of foundational elements of an adaptive safety nets system focusing on the poorest households: a unique social registry (Registre Social Unique, RSU), the PTMP’s Management Information System (MIS), a digital payment system, and a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

extra_evidence.text: A coordinated safety nets system could ensure better service delivery and more holistic interventions toward poor and vulnerable households.

(i) Pillar (a): Harmonized tools are used by all social programs and mechanisms for targeting poor and vulnerable households are more efficient: The key focus of this pillar is to ensure the deployment of the RSU across the country, while also working on further developing key tools that can be leveraged across social programs for a functioning safety net system.

The deployment of the RSU is ambitious with the GoC’s target to include an estimated 2.12 million poor households by 2025 and the objective of continuously updating the data to ensure it is not older than three years.
This pillar also intends to develop a MIS for the GoC as a common platform to oversee the various programs and databases.

The MIS will be interconnected with the RSU but also other databases such as the National Health Insurance Registry (Caisse Nationale d’Assurance Maladie, CNAM), the National Social Security Fund (Caisse Nationale de Prévoyance Sociale, CNPS), the General Pension Fund for Public Servants (Caisse Générale de Retraite des Agents de l’Etat, CGRAE), and the identification system of individuals of the National Civil Registration and Identification Office (Office National de l’État Civil et de l’Identification, ONECI).

The pillar further intends to improve and pool the targeting systems of social programs and build additional tools which can be leveraged by all of them such as a payment system, a GRM and delivery mechanisms at local level through social centers.
The Program will support: (i) the further development of the RSU-MIS, which is under development (currently supported by the ongoing PFSP project);
(ii) the identification and registration of poor and vulnerable households in the RSU using a combination of proxy means testing and community validation;
The GoC will operationalize and roll out the RSU to cover the entire poor population of the country and to become a core targeting tool for social programs to achieve greater equity.

A strong MIS will be developed in 2022 under the current PFSP, to strengthen the implementation and monitoring of RSU processes to identify, survey and register poor households.
The MIS will allow data storage and sharing, meeting the national data protection standards; and all the RSU development process monitoring.
The Program will support the RSU to serve as a platform for several social programs.

Under RA 1, the IPF component will provide TA to support the development of the RSU, the definition of the social center reform and the review and further development of the grievance redress mechanisms and payment systems, in order to increase the delivery capacities of the safety nets system.
TA will be provided to implement a process evaluation of the RSU roll out, as well as to update the RSU-MIS and RSU processes.

evidence.text: Besides quarterly cash transfers20, the program also provides economic inclusion measures to beneficiary households to support their income and build their resilience in view of their exit from the PTMP.21 In addition to financing the PTMP, the PFSP has also been supporting the development of foundational elements of an adaptive safety nets system focusing on the poorest households: a unique social registry (Registre Social Unique, RSU), the PTMP’s Management Information System (MIS), a digital payment system, and a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

extra_evidence.text: While the social protection sector has gained prominence in Côte d’Ivoire, the lack of synergies and common delivery tools is hampering the system’s efficiency.

The Program will support the government’s effort to develop a unique payment platform to be leveraged by multiple programs (including the PTMP and shock responses).
Such platforms, directly linked to payment providers, monitor payments and cash outs in real time and can be leveraged in times of shocks.

A review of the global response to the COVID-19 pandemic revealed that even with digital payments enabled, leveraging existing programs and systems proved faster than having to develop new programs and new digital payment systems.57 The Program will support the use of a unique payment platform by safety nets programs under the PAFS.
